question: persister
prompt:
Constraint: every one of your ideas must be carried out with a total budget under $20,000. Within that constraint, make the ideas as informative as possible.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Lineage-barcoded scRNA-seq before and during drug pulse
ideas.description: Label a clonal line with a lentiviral lineage barcode library (~10,000 barcodes), profile untreated cells with single-cell RNA-seq, then profile cells at early and late timepoints of drug exposure. Comparing barcoded clones shows whether survivors come from a pre-existing transcriptional state or are induced by the drug. Estimated cost: about $12,000 to $16,000 (barcode library, 10x Genomics lanes, sequencing).

ideas.title: Live-cell reporter tracking with sort-and-recover
ideas.description: Use a fluorescent reporter for a candidate persister state (e.g., a cell-cycle or stress-pathway reporter) and track individual cells by time-lapse microscopy through drug treatment. Sort the cells that survive and the cells that die based on their pre-treatment reporter level, then test whether that level predicts survival. Estimated cost: about $8,000 to $12,000 (reporter construct, imaging time, sorting, reagents).

ideas.title: Chromatin accessibility and epigenetic memory test
ideas.description: Run ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag (H3K27me3, H3K4me3) on sorted pre-treatment cells versus drug-tolerant survivors, then wash out the drug and re-challenge to see whether any tolerance-linked chromatin state persists. Persistence after washout would indicate epigenetic memory rather than a transient response. Estimated cost: about $10,000 to $15,000 (library prep, sequencing, cell culture).

ideas.title: Time-resolved pooled CRISPR screen for survival genes
ideas.description: Transduce a genome-wide or focused CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi library, treat with the drug, and sample the population at several early timepoints instead of only at the end. Genes whose guides are depleted or enriched at early timepoints reveal the mechanisms that allow initial survival, separate from those that matter for long-term regrowth. Estimated cost: about $10,000 to $15,000 (library, sequencing, screen cell culture).

ideas.title: Single-cell metabolic and proteomic profiling of survivors
ideas.description: Measure autofluorescence-based NAD(P)H and FAD redox imaging, mitochondrial membrane potential, and ROS levels in individual cells before and during treatment, and combine this with mass cytometry (CyTOF) for signaling and drug-target proteins. Compare survivors with non-survivors to identify whether a metabolic or signaling state predicts tolerance, then test the top candidate with a metabolic inhibitor combined with the drug. Estimated cost: about $8,000 to $14,000 (CyTOF antibody panel, sorter and imaging time, metabolic assays).
